# Google SecOps CTF

O3 Cyber and Google are excited to invite you to a morning of technical deep-dives and hands-on competition at the O3C office in Oslo on May 7th

2 min•Apr 22, 2026•By Olav Østbye

Image: Olav Østbye

O3 Cyber and Google are excited to invite you to a morning of technical deep-dives and hands-on competition at the O3C office in Oslo on May 7th. This session is designed for practitioners who want to move beyond legacy monitoring and experience the next generation of detection and response. Google SecOps is a cloud-native security operations platform built to empower teams to detect and respond to threats at machine speed. 

The CTF is an interactive, technical challenge using Google SecOps to detect and mitigate real-world attacks through Gemini AI-assisted workflows. Participants will master platform capabilities ranging from raw log analysis to structured Unified Data Model (UDM) searches for high-performance threat hunting and alert validation.

Two prizes will be awarded: one for the CTF winner and one via a random draw among all participants.

Venue & Date
O3C Office (Ground Floor), Schweigaards gate 46, 0191 Oslo
Thursday, May 7, 2026.

Logistics & Catering
Please bring a laptop and charger for the technical session. 
Complimentary breakfast will be served at 08:15, and refreshments and snacks will remain available throughout the event.

Registration & Selection
Due to limited capacity and the technical focus of the event, we are curating the attendee list. Priority is given to clients and potential clients of Google and O3 Cyber. Use the link below to register for the event.

# Silent Signer (#19)

S.N.A.F.U. agents recovered `sst-fwsign` from a compromised workstation inside the SST Dynamics factory. It appears to be part of the firmware signing pipeline that M4terM4xima uses to flash compromised firmware onto the robots. Our field analysts tried attaching a debugger: each time, the validation fails. Reverse the binary and recover the signing token it accepts.

N.B.: The binary requires root privileges but is harmless. If you're not comfortable running it as root, use a VM.

**What is a CTF?**

If you’re new to this, a CTF is a hacking contest where you solve puzzles to find a specific file, usually something like `secret.txt` or `flag.txt,` hidden on a server or inside a piece of code.

Once you find the file and read the "flag" inside, you get points! It’s the best way to practice real-world security skills in a fun, safe environment.
